text: Between 2021 and 2024, Senegalese security forces routinely used excessive and lethal force against protesters; Amnesty International and other civil-society organizations counted at least 65 people killed, the majority by firearms, with at least 1,000 wounded and a further 2,000 arrested.
short: Senegal 2021–2024: at least 65 protesters killed, 2,000 arrested (Amnesty)

source.name: Amnesty International: Senegal — Authorities must deliver justice to victims of violent repression of protests since 2021
source.quote: security forces routinely deployed excessive and lethal use of force against protesters. According to figures gathered by Amnesty International and other civil society organizations, at least 65 people were killed
source.note: Amnesty's statement on the first anniversary of Senegal's 2024 amnesty law; the same release says a further 2,000 people were arrested and at least 1,000 wounded.

additionalSources.name: Human Rights Watch — World Report 2024, Senegal chapter
additionalSources.quote: During 2023, arbitrary arrests of opposition figures and activists, security force use of excessive force, unjustified restrictions on civic space, and other human rights violations continued in Senegal.
additionalSources.note: HRW's chapter also records the interior minister putting the June 2023 violence at 16 deaths and 500 arrests, and the arrests of journalists and opposition leaders.
